topics.label: Opening framing and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by outlining the main learning outcomes and linking the upcoming material to previous histopathology practicals.

topics.label: Tumour virology and experimental assays for cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the historical investigation of transforming viruses established the cellular origin of proto-oncogenes and provided laboratory assays for assessing transformed cell phenotypes.

topics.label: Classification and genetic mechanisms of oncogenes and tumour suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer-associated mutations in oncogenes and tumour suppressor pathways alter cell cycle regulation and cellular phenotypes depending on allele dosage.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genomic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the distinct failures in DNA repair, DNA replication, and mitotic chromosome segregation that generate sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis, hereditary predispositions, and tumour evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how the sequential accumulation of somatic mutations and inherited genetic predispositions drive tumour development and ongoing malignancy.

topics.label: Closing framing and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a review of learning outcomes, recommended further reading, and housekeeping for the next session.
